induced_from: train split only, n=1200, seed=taxonomy:AmericanAir, TF-IDF + KMeans k=20, clusters named by LLM, merged by hand
tie_break_rule: 27.6% of training messages match two or more intent keyword rules. When a message carries more than one intent, label the one the customer wants ACTION on. If no action is requested, label the topic they lead with. Sentiment is never an intent: an angry message about a lost bag is track_baggage, not complain_service.
other_rule: Use `other` only when no other label applies, not when the message is unclear. Unclear messages still get their best-fit label and are flagged `ambiguous` in the golden set.

intents.name: report disruption
intents.description: The flight is delayed, cancelled, diverted, or the customer is stuck on the aircraft or has missed a connection. They want acknowledgement, an explanation, or an ETA - not, yet, a specific remedy.
intents.positive: three hour delay? You guys r trashhhhhhh
intents.near_miss: There is none. Rebook me. I am getting off
intents.near_miss_why: A disruption is the cause, but the customer is asking for a specific remedy, which is a different action for the agent.

intents.name: rebook or reroute
intents.description: The customer explicitly asks to be moved to a different flight, put on standby, rerouted, or have their itinerary changed because of a disruption.
intents.positive: I just missed a flight so had to cancel and rebook - can you get me on the next one to DFW
intents.near_miss: Now my 7:15 flight is showing 7:55 because of a late flight attendant
intents.near_miss_why: Reports the problem but makes no request to be moved.

intents.name: track baggage
intents.description: Anything about a bag: lost, delayed, damaged, a forced gate-check, or a carry-on dispute.
intents.positive: Are you kidding me?! You make me check my bag and then it comes out on the belt like this?!
intents.near_miss: why would they make me pay for my ONE CARRY ON SIZE bag when I didn't pay for it on my first flight
intents.near_miss_why: The bag is the subject, but the customer is disputing a fee rule, not reporting a bag problem.

intents.name: request refund or compensation
intents.description: The customer wants money, miles, a voucher, or reimbursement - for a fare, a fee, an expense caused by a disruption, or as goodwill.
intents.positive: you should be reimbursing the hotel bill you made us foot for the missed connection
intents.near_miss: how do you see if a flight was booked with refundable tickets? Doesn't say on the app
intents.near_miss_why: Asks how refundability works; does not request a refund.

intents.name: manage booking
intents.description: Seat assignment or upgrade, check-in, boarding pass, name correction, or any change to an existing reservation that is not caused by a disruption.
intents.positive: What a great window seat. Why can't a prompt be set when you choose 10A?
intents.near_miss: There is none. Rebook me. I am getting off..need upgrade
intents.near_miss_why: Driven by a disruption, so the remedy is a rebooking, not routine seat management.

intents.name: ask policy or information
intents.description: A question about rules, fees, allowances, procedures, or the status of a flight the customer is not currently disrupted by. Answerable from published information.
intents.positive: Will that TSA form be sufficient enough to be able to check-in/check my bag tomorrow morning?
intents.near_miss: Can we please get an update on our flight Dallas to MKE. No one seems to know anything
intents.near_miss_why: Phrased as a question, but the customer is in a live disruption and wants acknowledgement.

intents.name: complain about service
intents.description: Dissatisfaction with staff, crew, ground handling, or the airline generally, with no specific remedy requested and no other intent present.
intents.positive: truly awful customer service and your ground staff blaming another airline is unacceptable
intents.near_miss: Never flying with you again. Just received my bag 2 mins ago.
intents.near_miss_why: Angry in tone, but the subject is a bag, and the tie-break rule says sentiment is never the intent.

intents.name: praise service
intents.description: Thanks, compliments, or a shout-out to staff. Includes gratitude after a problem was solved.
intents.positive: Your rep, Jacki, here at ORD helped me get home tonight. Thanks for the response!
intents.near_miss: Thanks for a 5 hour delay to start the week off. #platinumlife
intents.near_miss_why: Sarcasm. The literal word 'thanks' is not praise; read the intent, not the token.

intents.name: ask about loyalty programme
intents.description: AAdvantage miles, elite status, boarding group, lounge access, or benefits tied to status.
intents.positive: Hit Gold status and I'm still Group 6? What gives? What's the benefit of Gold?
intents.near_miss: Anyone with American Aadvantage miles they won't use and would like to gift?
intents.near_miss_why: Addressed to other users, not a request to the airline.

intents.name: other
intents.description: Anything else: chit-chat, photos, news commentary, messages aimed at other users, marketing, or content that is not a support request at all.
intents.near_miss: Kudos to the pilot that had the smoothest landing I've experienced
intents.near_miss_why: Not a support request, but it is directed at the airline and is clearly praise.
